title: The Pattern
timelinePosition: Day 5 of the hunt from the grain road (Ch5 day count). The party left the carters' lodge at the fork at first light and turned onto the south road. S1 is early morning on the climb, S2 is late morning to early afternoon at the Strahnbrad camp, S3 is the afternoon run to Andorhal, which comes into sight in the last working hours of the day.
openLocation: Southern feeder road into Andorhal's network, with the Strahnbrad military zone ahead.
immediateObjective: Confirm how large the grain-plague plot really is and force someone in Lordaeron's command to take the warning seriously.
constraints: Limited third, absolute: Jaina only. Nothing she cannot see, hear, feel, read or infer. Sylvanas is read from outside.
Register change from Ch5 (paper, ledgers, night road): Ch6 is camp, rank, noise, mud, then a living city. Do not re-run ledger work or the sickroom.

Narration for Sylvanas: Ch5 moved Sylvanas's own narration to 'Jaina' for the mage. Aloud, Sylvanas still says 'Mage' (or 'Proudmoore' in front of others) unless this outline changes it; it does not. Lyriel says 'Jaina'; Cyndia does not.

Jaina's body: right hand dead since Ch2, left hand raw and wrapped with two usable fingertips. Reins and the notes are held in the left hand or against the saddle. No casual inking, no hand-reading. Readings come through spell light, the staff, or pressure in her head. Carry fatigue: little rest since the Ch4 vigil.

Jaina's magical sensitivity is the only way the party perceives contamination. Elves cannot feel it. Sylvanas's question in Beat 7 ('did you read anything off him') is a legitimate use of that and must have a real, quick, honest answer: nothing but a tired clerk.

Arthas is read from outside through behavior, voice, and what others lose around him. Warm, confident, charismatic at Strahnbrad (character sheet), courteous used as a shield. Not cartoon cruelty. Part of his reasoning must be understandable: the orc war is real and visible.
Do not claim Arthas ignores her out of personal cruelty alone. The orc war matters. Do not flatten him into a villain or Jaina into a victim.
No Mal'Ganis naming or recognition. No Kel'Thuzad naming; Jaina's 'someone I once studied with' is a fear she cannot test, not a name.
No certainty that the Barovs designed the plague. Barov paperwork is connection, not guilt (carried from Ch5). Do not re-explain the Barov name or the lost day; they are callbacks.

The farewell ('May the stars keep your road') is a plant: Sylvanas calls it wrong, not yet a pattern. Do not explain it in prose. The tally-man must read as helpful, ordinary, forgettable on the surface.
Cyndia's turned head at the Millhaven carter is held for Ch9. In Beat 7 Cyndia may be present on the road but must not react to or connect the farewell on the page.
Lyriel's Ch3 answer about the carter must not be connected by any character to the farewell, the depot warning, or the tally-man.
Havel is not known to be cult-paid by any character. The party takes him as a militia captain who knows the granary district. The second read is planter-only, never narrated as fact.
Neral is not with the party. She stays on the northbound warning line.
Do not state that all human authority is useless everywhere. It fails here, at this camp, in this hour.
No counted time in dialogue ('two breaths'). Orders by event.

Jaina's ladder (plague-mechanism.md, Ch4-6): she isolates ingestion, repeated exposure and body participation as a design. She still cannot explain how sickness becomes undeath. Do not hand her the 'answering chamber' model or low/high fidelity; that is Ch9-12.
No pre-written dialogue in plan beyond the two locked lines recorded below. The plague line in Beat 1 and the farewell in Beat 7 are authorial anchors from the outline.

Sylvanas carries the evidence at the open. At the Ch5 fork she folded the shared map sheet (knife hole at Strahnbrad) and put it in her coat with the Barov slips and the ANDORHAL sacking square. Any paper Jaina holds up to Arthas has to pass from Sylvanas's coat to Jaina's hand on the page before B4. Jaina holds it in the two bare fingertips of the wrapped left hand or pinned against the staff. She cannot write new notes.

Ch5 closed on a long brown smear moving over the hills, 'too brown for mist'. It is army traffic dust or smoke from the burned farms, never plague. It should resolve as the army by the time the camp is in view (B3). Morning mist low on the road in B1 can sit under it.

Arthas's war is against orcs 'out of the camps' burning farms in the hills. That came from the Ch5 road talk at the south-road inn, and Jaina was at that table. The outline's Blackrock raiders are those orcs. His war is the camps' war, and B5's memory turns on that. The burned farms and the dead are real.

Sylvanas 'knows there is history' only from what she sees (subplot-jaina-arthas.md). The internment-camp memory in B5 stays inside Jaina. She does not tell it to Sylvanas; the Arthas price is told at sea in Ch19.
No named Silver Hand or army officers besides Arthas: no Uther, no Falric. They are not in the outline cast. The Silver Hand is plate and tabards in the camp.
No party member gives a road blessing or an ornate farewell (Lyriel and Cyndia voice-sheet rule). The farewell belongs to the tally-man alone.
The tally-man must not resemble the Ch3 carter: no crooked nose, no hat turned in the hands, no brown cob or flat wagon. He is on foot. His face stays forgettable.

Jaina cannot read people. In Ch5 she read the overseer: 'Nothing on him... No more than on you.' Her 'nothing' in B7 is the same limit. She does not connect the tally-man to the overseer, and she does not know Sylvanas has been turning the carter over since Ch5 (that was Sylvanas's interior).
The river-depot overseer fled south with his wife (Ch5). Do not sight him on this road.

Ch4 already put the built-craft recognition on the page: 'It's made. Somebody very good made this.', the locked shelf in Dalaran, wanting to take it apart, 'as Antonidas built a ward'. S1 is the next step. The whole system is the weapon, with the body inside it, and the fear points at a person trained where she was. Give the Ch4 material brief anchors only. Do not re-run the shelf exposition.

Name usage. Aloud, Jaina says 'Ranger-General' to Sylvanas and 'Arthas' to the prince, from old habit. Arthas says 'Jaina' to her and 'Ranger-General' to Sylvanas. Sylvanas says 'Proudmoore' in front of others and 'Mage' otherwise. To Arthas she uses his correct title, said precisely. Jaina's narration calls her 'Sylvanas'.

povKnowsAtOpen: The cult is organized, watched, and disciplined.
Barov property and paperwork keep turning up in the trail of rot.
Their chosen road runs through the military zone near Strahnbrad before Andorhal.
Her sensitivity has put them ahead of most of Lordaeron, but they are still chasing poison that has already spread.
The old carter from the Millhaven road is still an unresolved road clue in her mind.
They lost a day to a depot overseer's lie.
She can see necromancy in the design but cannot explain how sickness becomes undeath.
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: Whether the Barovs are fully complicit.
What Andorhal looks like from inside the city.
mustNotBeImpliedYet: No certainty that the Barovs designed the plague.
No claim that Arthas ignores her out of personal cruelty alone. The orc war matters.
No claim that all human authority is useless everywhere rather than failing here.
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Arthas heard the warning and chose the visible war first.
Sylvanas has heard the farewell twice and calls it wrong, not yet a pattern. Jaina got no magical read off the man, and he was gone before Sylvanas looked back.
The plague is deliberate, formally trained craft, with the body part of the mechanism. Origin and ladder height unknown.
A granary tally-man told them to ask for Captain Havel at the militia post by the market gate.
Andorhal looks alive and busy even though the plagued roads run through it.

pov: She opens convinced clear evidence will make Arthas act before Andorhal locks down.
She keeps pushing facts as if proof and rank should matter more than the visible war in front of him.
Arthas hears her out and still turns to the orcs, forcing her to accept Sylvanas was right about the army.
By the end, Jaina stops looking to Lordaeron's command for rescue and turns toward Andorhal itself.

beats: Sylvanas reads the soldiers, the hierarchy, and the coming refusal faster than Jaina does.
Jaina keeps hoping proof will prove Sylvanas too cynical, then watches Sylvanas call the prince's blindness before the conversation is over.
Their argument no longer feels like mage versus soldier. It feels like two women reading the same failure from different angles.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They are still strained, but they are finally working the same problem.
The fight over whether Lordaeron will listen ends here, and their anger turns outward.
They are not gentle with each other yet, but the old prejudice has less room to hide.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: still with the riding party.
Lyriel: still with the riding party.
Neral: not with the party. She remains on the northbound warning line after escorting the survivor girl out.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 7 opens at Andorhal with the same four riders arriving to hunt the poison's source.

chapterBridge.previousChapterClose: Ch5 ends in Sylvanas's POV at first light on day 5. At the carters' lodge at the fork, Sylvanas pins Strahnbrad with her knife and turns down Jaina's offer of a re-read ('No'). She warns that the army will put the flour after the orcs and 'Expect them to get in the way.' Jaina: 'Then I'll have to show it to them.' Sylvanas: 'You'll have to. I can't see it either.' Sylvanas folds the sheet into her coat with the slips and the sacking. The four ride out in the old order, turn south onto the bending road between the hedges, and see a long brown smear moving over the hills ahead, too brown for mist.
chapterBridge.continuityOfState: Same morning, a few hours later, the same four riders in the same order. Jaina slept sitting against a stone block for part of the night. She is grey and cold from the fork reading: right arm dead with the staff in its crook, left hand wrapped with two bare fingertips, and she ate Lyriel's burnt crust in two fingers. Sylvanas carries the sheet, the Barov slips and the ANDORHAL square. Jaina has accepted the job of showing it to the army.
chapterBridge.informationAsymmetry: This is the first time inside Jaina since Ch4. She does not know that Sylvanas thinks 'Jaina' now, that the old carter has been nagging Sylvanas, or that Cyndia turned her head at the farewell in Ch3. Sylvanas does not know the internment-camp night, or what Jaina believes her history with Arthas will buy.
chapterBridge.orientingAnchor: One anchor is enough. Either the road under the hooves, which Jaina chose and which now has to prove her right, or the brown smear ahead. Do not re-run the fork.
chapterBridge.intentionalJump: POV switch from Sylvanas back to Jaina, with a short time skip inside the same morning.

scene.title: The Road to Andorhal
scene.sceneFunction: The old carter clue resurfaces on the road, and Andorhal finally appears.
scene.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Arthas has failed them, and the city is their only remaining lead.

beats.goal: Get last directions into Andorhal from the first ordinary person walking out of it.
beats.conflict: He is helpful, ordinary, forgettable until his farewell. Sylvanas turns in the saddle at the words and asks whether Jaina read anything off him. Jaina got nothing but a tired clerk. By the time Sylvanas looks back, he is lost in the traffic.

outcome.summary: They get usable directions: ask at the militia post by the market gate for Captain Havel, who knows the granary district. The farewell from Millhaven comes back and leaves Sylvanas with a wrong note she cannot use yet. Twice is wrong, but not yet a pattern. She says so in a few words and rides on.

beats.valueShift: plain courtesy -> a wrong note Jaina cannot read
newOnPageInformation: A granary tally-man walking out of Andorhal with a ledger satchel gave directions
Ask at the militia post by the market gate for Captain Havel, who knows the granary district better than anyone
He glanced back up the road toward Andorhal's granary roofs as he answered
He sent them off with the farewell from Millhaven (locked line: May the stars keep your road)
Sylvanas heard the farewell a second time, asked whether Jaina read anything, and called it wrong but not yet a pattern
stillUnknownAfterBeat: That it is the same being in another face
sensoryAnchors: a ledger satchel, its strap worn pale across his coat
the chill of hearing the words a second time
Sylvanas twisted in the saddle toward a road full of strangers
beats.interiority: nothing off him but a tired clerk, and she looked properly, didn't she; Sylvanas turned in the saddle over a turn of phrase; a farewell is a farewell; but she was asked, and had nothing, and dislikes having nothing
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas carries the beat. Cyndia and Lyriel present and silent about the phrase (Cyndia's carter reaction is held for Ch9; Lyriel must not connect anything).
beats.plannerWarning: Planter and POV tension: the second read is information Jaina does not have. The writer must render the glance and the look as ordinary behaviour (a man sizing up armed strangers on elven horses) and not tilt the narration toward suspicion.
beats.transitionIntent: sensory-carry: the farewell stays with Sylvanas as a wrong note and the road to Andorhal narrows.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, afternoon. The last stretch before Andorhal, with foot and cart traffic thickening on the road.
beats.continuityNote: The wording is fixed: 'May the stars keep your road.' Jaina was present at Millhaven in Ch3, but that was Sylvanas's POV, so Jaina has no on-page memory of the phrase. It reaches her through Sylvanas's turn in the saddle. Jaina does not know Sylvanas has been turning the carter over since Ch5, so the turn looks out of proportion to her. 'Did you read anything' is a real use of Jaina's sense, and the answer is honest: she cannot read people (Ch5, the overseer). She does not draw the overseer parallel herself. Lyriel, who answered the carter in Ch3, connects nothing. Cyndia shows no reaction on the page (held for Ch9). The order of march he looks over: Sylvanas in front, Cyndia on the left, Lyriel on the right at Jaina's knee, Jaina in the middle, two places at the back. Render the look only as a man sizing up armed strangers on elven horses. Craft research, fair play: the clue is on the page, ordinary, and followed at once by something more pressing (B8's body reaction).

beats.goal: Keep riding toward Andorhal while the city's magical rot presses on her.
beats.conflict: The closer they get, the less she can keep the plague at arm's length. The corruption becomes a physical reaction. The horses feel it before the buildings show and go skittish on the narrowing road.

outcome.summary: Jaina keeps riding anyway. The corruption is heavy enough to force a body reaction, and they push on until the city breaks the horizon.

beats.valueShift: theory at a distance -> pain in her body
newOnPageInformation: Andorhal's magical rot stops being theory and hurts Jaina physically
The horses sense it before the buildings are visible
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether Andorhal is already dead behind its walls
sensoryAnchors: the horses sidestep as at the ring stones and do not settle after
the staff crystal dimming, frost rising on the two bare fingertips
beats.interiority: the plague was theory for most of the road and the road is done arguing with her; she keeps riding because stopping is no different from waiting on permission
beats.castFunction: Thalassian horses are trained to settle near arcane hum (thalassian-horses.md); here they do not settle. Sylvanas and Cyndia work the animals. Lyriel is at Jaina's knee, and when Lyriel checks on her, Jaina keeps going. That is the agency in the beat: stopping would be waiting again.
beats.transitionIntent: action-continuation: they keep riding until the city breaks the horizon.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, late afternoon. The road narrowing into Andorhal's approach, the city not yet in sight.
beats.continuityNote: This is the next rung of the horse ladder. At the ring stones in Ch1-2 they sidestepped once and stood. In Millhaven in Ch3 the mare backed and pinned her ears. Here they sidestep and never settle. It is also the next rung of Jaina's cost ladder from Ch5: teeth chattering, frost on the bare fingertips, the crystal dimming through the day. She can feel Andorhal now only because she is physically arriving; she cannot hear places she has not been (Ch5). Elves still feel nothing themselves. They read it off the horses and off Jaina.

beats.goal: Reach sight of Andorhal and learn whether it is a ruin or a living city.
beats.conflict: They expected a ruin and the rot and body reaction primed her for one. What she sees is a working city with granaries moving, traffic flowing, ordinary commercial noise and something rotten underneath.

outcome.summary: Andorhal is worse than a ruin: it is working. The plague runs through a living hub, and whoever manages the spread is still inside. Chapter 7 opens with the ride into the city.

beats.valueShift: expecting a dead town -> seeing a living machine at the center
newOnPageInformation: Andorhal is trading and functioning, not dead
The poisoned roads converge on a working hub
Whoever manages the spread is likely still inside the walls
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Who inside the walls is directing the spread
sensoryAnchors: wagons in lines on the approach
beats.interiority: the city looks alive and that is the horror; they were chasing something that had already spread, and it was running; whoever manages it is still in there; nobody behind her is coming, and the city is the thing in front of her
beats.transitionIntent: planted question: who inside the walls is running it. Chapter 7 (Sylvanas POV) opens with the ride in and the one name they have, Captain Havel at the market-gate militia post.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, late afternoon into the last working hours. Granaries and traffic still moving.
beats.continuityNote: Andorhal has been a name since Ch4 (Brask: 'the big granaries'; the ANDORHAL stencil) and a hub on paper since Ch5 (Andorhal at one end of every readable slip). This is the first sight of it. Since Ch3, the places ahead have been alive and trading while the sickness spreads through them; this is the same pattern at full scale. The party is coming in by the back way, the south road, not the King's road and its front gate. Close on Jaina facing the city, which lands POV arc bullet 4. Craft research, arrival: the city is filtered through what Jaina's body already knows, one concise picture, then out.

factsLocked: Arthas heard the warning and did not act on it the way they needed.
Sylvanas has heard the farewell twice and calls it wrong, not yet a pattern. Jaina got no magical read off the man, and he was gone before Sylvanas looked back.
The party reaches Andorhal by the road chosen in Chapter 5.
A granary tally-man on the road told them to ask for Captain Havel at the militia post by the market gate.
The city still looks alive and busy even though the plague roads run through it.
factsNotEarned: Any claim that all human authority is useless everywhere rather than failing here.
